cards.summary: Cognition (the strongest contrarian) argues shared context matters for parallel writers, but its own April 2026 update says fresh context works best for independent reviewers and that the objection targets parallel-writer swarms. A sequential, single-writer, file-and-git-state harness is outside the target of the critique. Direct controlled evidence for fresh-process-per-unit vs one long session on Claude 5 is missing.

contrarian.claim: Share context between agents; fragmented context yields conflicting decisions
contrarian.note: Only the search snippet was seen, not the full essay. Argument is about parallel agents making implicit conflicting choices; not a measured study.

contrarian.claim: Original observations still hold for parallel-writer swarms; narrower patterns work; fresh-context reviewer works best; share context otherwise
contrarian.note: Fetched. Says reviewer 'works best when coding and review agents do not share any context'; ties context rot to long contexts; also warns agents wrongly assume shared state with children. No quantitative data.

contrarian.claim: Multi-agent systems cost ~15x chat tokens; coding has fewer parallelizable subtasks and needs shared context
contrarian.note: Vendor-run, research (not coding) workload. Cost is for parallel multi-agent, not sequential fresh-session pipelines. Same post endorses summarise-to-files and spawning fresh subagents with handoff.

contrarian.claim: Subagent handoff is the largest failure category (41.8%) and often silent
contrarian.note: Read-only repo QA, deep agentic search with planner->subagent. Shows handoff loss is real; narrower than SDLC stage handoffs.

failures.what: Claude Code users report loss of working knowledge after context reset/compaction (retries known-bad approach, wrong identifiers) despite state saved in files
failures.whatItShows: Files alone do not guarantee the successor reads them; the packet must force reading. Supports the owner's script-printed packets design rather than refuting fresh context.

conditions: Holds for sequential single-writer stages where state lives in files/git and the script injects what to read
Fails or degrades for parallel writers making interdependent design choices
Fresh reviewers help (Cognition); fresh implementers lose tacit decisions unless recorded
Cost: re-reading per stage; no measured Claude 5 comparison found
cards.conclusion: No credible evidence refutes fresh-context-per-unit for a sequential script-driven harness; the main contrarian evidence addresses parallel writers and the author later narrowed it. The real risk is silent knowledge loss at handoff, which argues for explicit state files and script-enforced reading, not for abandoning fresh contexts. Verdict would shift if a controlled study showed a long-session Opus 5 beating fresh-per-stage on end-to-end SDLC tasks at equal cost; none found.

cards.summary: Degradation with length persists in 2025-2026 measurements, but it is task- and context-type dependent: a Sept 2026 test shows Opus 5 flat with unrelated padding to 500k yet losing ~15% of solved tasks with task-related context. Hard fill-fraction thresholds (30-50%) are unsupported; the best-known anecdotes are model self-reports.

contrarian.claim: Opus 5 is robust to irrelevant context up to 500k tokens (0.50/0.52/0.48 pass rate)
contrarian.note: 20 terminal-bench tasks, small N, within-noise caveats. Also shows related context drops Opus 5 from 0.50 to 0.43/0.40; authors recommend fresh sessions or compaction. Mixed: supports and limits the card.

contrarian.claim: Chroma's context rot tests are simple, only two haystack topics, no mechanism; real-world may differ
contrarian.note: Fetched. Claude showed lowest hallucination, mostly abstaining; no Claude 5 data; no study of 30-50% fill.

contrarian.claim: Opus 4.6 1M context: MRCR v2 76% at 1M, 93% at 256K; long context usable
contrarian.note: Only seen through search summaries, not fetched; no Opus 5 MRCR figure found.

failures.what: Opus 4.6 1M user reports degradation from ~20-40% fill; thresholds are the model's own statements
failures.whatItShows: Practitioner folklore, no repro; weak evidence for specific percentages.

failures.what: Chroma: all 18 models degrade with length even on simple tasks; focused 300-token prompt beats 113k full prompt on LongMemEval
failures.whatItShows: Degradation is real but earlier-era; magnitude for Claude 5 unmeasured here.

conditions: Irrelevant padding hurts Opus 5 little; relevant but distracting accumulated task context hurts more
Sizing units to a modest fraction of context is cheap insurance but the specific fraction is unsupported
Cognition 2026 also asserts context rot at long contexts (anecdotal)
cards.conclusion: Direction is supported by the only Opus-5-era controlled test (relevant context lost ~15% of solved tasks at 250k), so sizing units well under the window is sound. The justification should be framed as 'accumulated task-related context degrades pass rate' rather than a fixed fill threshold, and no data supports a 30-50% cutoff. Larger controlled agentic tests on Opus 5/Sonnet 5 showing flat performance would weaken it.

cards.summary: Lossy-summary failures are well documented in Claude Code issues and in a vendor eval where artifact tracking scored ~2.3/5, and JetBrains found simple observation masking matches LLM summarisation (on older/open models, SWE-bench). But handoff via authored files is a different mechanism from automatic transcript compaction, and no study shows raw transcripts beating a purpose-written handoff.

contrarian.claim: Observation masking matches LLM summarisation at about half the cost of raw; summaries elongate trajectories 13-15%
contrarian.who: Lindenbauer et al., JetBrains Research / TUM
contrarian.note: SWE-bench Verified, five configs; neither strategy consistently wins; for Gemini 2.5 Flash thinking, raw 40.4, masking 36.4, summary 31.4 (both below raw). Tests within-session context management, not cross-context handoff.

contrarian.claim: Compaction summaries drop critical details; artifact trail weak for every method
contrarian.note: 36k production messages; Factory scored itself best; artifact tracking 2.19-2.45/5 for all methods; no variance reported.

contrarian.claim: Object-aware retention differs; budgets do not equal delivered context; calibration gains may not transfer

failures.what: Instructions and working knowledge lost after Claude Code compaction; 'follows rules perfectly before, violates after'
failures.whatItShows: Reproduction steps given but no measured rate; closed not planned. Other issues (24572, 9796, 31409, 22376) report same pattern, seen only via mirror site search results.

failures.what: Subagent handoff caused 41.8% of failures, often silent confident wrong answers
failures.whatItShows: Handoff is a leading failure site; narrow task type.

conditions: Authored, structured handoff with verified artifact paths beats automatic freeform summary
Handoff should point to files rather than paraphrase them
Preliminary Boolean result: compaction recovers some lost performance on Opus 5
Handoff failures are silent, so a script check that the successor read named files is needed
cards.conclusion: The claim that a handoff is lossy is supported, but it refutes naive summarisation, not a script-enforced handoff whose content lives in files. The JetBrains result suggests that dropping stale observations may be as good as summarising within a stage, which is irrelevant when context is cleared between stages. Unresolved: no controlled comparison of handoff note vs raw transcript on Claude 5; a harness-level A/B would settle it.

cards.summary: Anthropic's stated move to agentic search rests on 'internal vibes' by its own admission, while Cursor's measured data and a 2026 SWE-QA study show indexed retrieval beating or complementing agentic grep. A repo map is not an embedding index, and an ETH study found repository overviews unhelpful for coding agents, so the value of a budgeted map is unproven rather than refuted.

contrarian.claim: Agentic search generally works better than RAG with a local vector DB
contrarian.note: Fetched secondhand report; he said 'mostly vibes' plus internal benchmarks. Not a repo-map comparison.

contrarian.claim: Repository overviews in context files are not helpful for coding agents; context files add >20% cost with no success gain
contrarian.modelEra: early-2026 agents (models not named in abstract)
contrarian.note: Overviews, not script-built ranked maps; indirect. Developer-written files gave a marginal, non-significant gain.

contrarian.claim: No single retrieval family dominates; agentic trajectories miss every gold file on 27-35% of samples; RepoMap gives best context yield at 8K
contrarian.note: Abstract only. Favours repo map under tight token budgets: evidence for, not against.

failures.what: Cursor: semantic search added to grep raises answer accuracy 12.5% avg (6.5-23.5%) and cuts dissatisfaction; grep-only worse
failures.whatItShows: Vendor-run, but measured offline and A/B; pre-built index beats pure agentic grep. Index, not map.

failures.what: Semantic index search answered 65.2% of SWE-QA correctly vs 46.2% for deep agentic search, at under half the cost
failures.whatItShows: Contradicts 'agentic beats index' for read-only QA; subagent-based variant, not plain grep.

failures.what: Semantic search lifted file precision 65% to 87% on 50 ContextBench tasks but recall mixed and confounded with windowed reads

conditions: Map helps when repo is large and token budget tight
Pure agentic grep is the Anthropic default and works well for named symbols
Hybrid (map or index plus grep) is the best-supported pattern
No head-to-head test of Aider-style PageRank map vs agentic search on Claude 5 found
cards.conclusion: The 'agentic search beats indexes' claim is weakly evidenced (admitted vibes), and measured studies favour adding pre-built retrieval to grep, so the card is not refuted. However, direct evidence for a tree-sitter+PageRank map specifically is thin, and ETH found repo overviews unhelpful, so treat the map as an optional hint with a small budget and measure it in the harness. A paired run with and without the map on Sonnet 5 would decide it.
